blocks.block: [what] — the change, in the imperative and concrete: which artifact, which behaviour now differs. Not "improved things" — "extract _cycle_rollup, cmd_cycle 152 to 80 lines". The subject line is the headline; [what] is the precise diff in one or two sentences. The gate requires [what] present (amber if missing).

[why] — the trigger and the decision. What task or breakage forced this, and — when a fork was taken — which option was chosen and why the others were not. This is where a design decision (canon vs template, fix vs leash, the residuality verdict) is recorded so the next session inherits the reasoning, not just the outcome. A [why] that only restates [what] wasted the block.

[how] — the mechanism and the key insight: the approach that worked and WHY it worked when the obvious one did not. The one line that saves the next session thirty minutes of re-discovery lives here ("sensor cursors are STRINGS, not dicts"). Mechanism, not narration of every edit.

[test] — the verification evidence, replayable not quotable: the command run and its result/exit code, re-run AFTER the last edit (§verify-never-claim). "smoke green; unit 51 passed; doctor clean; index emits 1 commit-protocol chunk". An EMPTY [test] block is a verify-never-claim violation in writing — the gate warns on a [test] that reads like a claim ("should work") rather than evidence.

[broke] — the journey: what was tried and FAILED, and the real error text verbatim (never paraphrased — the exact string grep would find). Dead ends are the most valuable lines in the message: "Approach 1 failed because X" stops the next session repeating it. Empty only when nothing failed — and be honest, something usually does.

[next] — the baton: the single most important thing the next session should do, and any state still broken or deferred. A deferred shortcut names its follow-up task id here (§no-quick-fixes-without-a-leash). This is what the next session reads first.

discipline.rule: Never commit without the journey. "fix: resolved error" is worthless — what error, what caused it, what was tried first. Every session starts from zero; re-discovery is the number-one time killer. The commit that records the dead end is the one that saves the next session from walking into it.

Paste real error messages, verbatim — the exact string grep would find, the signal line not the full stack trace, never a paraphrase. A paraphrased error is ungreppable and therefore lost. This is the same rule as §verbatim-protocol applied to the log: the exact text carries signal a summary destroys.

Record what failed and why. "Approach 1: used RunRequest with partition_key directly to ERROR: requires asset_selection" prevents the next agent from trying it. Honesty over tidiness: a clean message that hides two failed approaches has thrown away the most useful thing the session learned.

One logical change per commit — atomic. Do not mix a doc edit, a bug fix, and an infra change in one commit. Each commit is a single reversible unit; mixing them makes [broke]/[next] ambiguous and makes a clean revert impossible.

Verification is non-negotiable: every commit records what was checked and whether it passed, in [test], re-run after the final edit. Evidence from a different session or from before the last change does not count (§verify-never-claim). The [test] block is the contract the commit-msg gate checks for evidence shape.

The log is queryable institutional memory. `git log --grep` mines it: by error string to find who hit it before, by scope to see a subsystem's whole journey, by "[broke]" to find every commit where something failed first. Writing the blocks well is what makes these queries return signal years later.

commit-protocol.enforcement: The commit-msg gate (`socom gate commit-msg`) is the mechanical floor: subject `type(scope): description` is RED (blocks), and missing [what] or [test] is amber (warns + logs a breach, never blocks) — velocity-first, the safe path stays the easy path (§psychological-acceptability). The four soft blocks ([why] [how] [broke] [next]) are deliberately NOT hard-checked: their value is judgement, not presence, and a gate that blocked on them would be routed around. This protocol documents their meaning so they are written well; the gate guarantees only the floor.
